questions.prompt: A direct HTTP/1.1 GET uses https://library.example:8443/books/7?edition=2#notes. Which target is correct?

options.label: Send /books/7?edition=2; keep #notes out of the HTTP target.
Send /home because the origin knows the desired book.

questions.explanation: For this direct origin-form request, the absolute path and query form the target. The fragment is handled separately. A proxy or CONNECT would require its own request-form review.

questions.prompt: Which component split preserves the original address?

options.label: The resource is a universal sixth component after the path.
The authority is library.example:8443; the path is /books/7.

questions.explanation: Authority includes the host and explicit port here. Path, query and fragment have distinct delimiters; the last path segment is not a separate universal component named resource.

questions.prompt: What does a URI establish without additional evidence?

options.label: Every URI must initiate an HTTP request.
A URI can identify without promising that retrieval will succeed.
Its representation is reachable and currently authorized.

questions.explanation: Identification does not promise a reachable representation or the current user permission. Naming and locating mechanisms need their own resolution and access evidence.

questions.prompt: The trace already has an eligible secured connection. What can the reviewer conclude?

options.label: A valid reusable connection can avoid a new handshake; record the actual path.
Every navigation still requires a new TCP and TLS handshake.
A reusable connection proves that no network work remains.

questions.explanation: Under the applicable reuse rules, setup may be avoided. The request and response still need evidence, and other navigations can take different cache, proxy or setup branches.

questions.prompt: HTML arrives successfully while an image fails and application loading is pending. Which receipt is accurate?

options.label: A 200 HTML response proves that the whole application is ready.
The image failure proves that no HTML was received.
A successful response is one stage; rendering and later requests have their own evidence.

questions.explanation: Response success, subresource results and the application-ready condition are separate stages. Preserve the observed success and failure instead of collapsing them into one page-ready claim.
